title: fix: omit numeric continuation metadata from centered history
body: ## What Problem This Solves `chat.history` adds numeric `hasMore` metadata to centered and retained cursor reads when an older source-bound cursor exists. These responses intentionally omit numeric paging metadata; clients continue with their source-bound cursors. ## User Impact Centered and retained reads keep their valid cursors and omit numeric continuation metadata. Default-tail and explicit-offset reads retain numeric continuation, including real exhaustion and response-budget trimming. The Control UI keeps its existing cursor-based history loading. ## Why This Change Was Made The response owner now selects numeric metadata from the page's numeric pagination capability. Cursor availability is independent of that capability. The reader's exhausted-prefix result and response-byte trimming still determine whether a numeric page has older rows. This preserves the landed numeric continuation and hidden-gap repairs in #188488 and #188557. It restores the original centered omission assertion and strengthens the existing retained-reset scenario without adding test lines. Cursor generation, admission, storage and asynchronous ownership are unchanged. The existing client documentation already describes this contract. ## Evidence - Current-target production fails the protected centered Gateway assertion and retained-cursor omission assertion; its byte-trimmed numeric preservation control passes. - All **307 affected Gateway, worker, import, embedded and TUI cases pass**, including the complete older-walk/no-loss tails, cursor/byte/fragment bounds, hidden/tool-only exhaustion and malformed/stale/wrong-session refusal. - All **12 selected UI unit/browser cases pass**, including the full normal history-loading suite. - All **8 existing serialized RPC request-budget cases pass**. - All **38 selected type graphs**, changed-file formatting/lint and the unchanged zero-growth test-line guard pass. This is focused proof; hosted CI supplies broad coverage. UI fixtures demonstrate preservation of the normal history-loading path; real Gateway/RPC tests establish the response contract. ## Visual evidence []() | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Historical baseline: both older messages loaded using source\-bound cursors](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13846871-af52-4bfd-bd53-07cb34bf9a51) | ![Exact candidate: both older messages remain visible after cursor back\-scroll](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13846871-af52-4bfd-bd53-07cb34bf9a51) | ### Exact\-head upward wheel and older\-message loading https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/00adaeaa-4239-41aa-825b-38022fe9bb29 ### Visual verification - Baseline: 4591070b2f4b1b043b57c306fcd6d235e56b04a2 \(historical pre\-repair UI, tree e112d34487864cb5d2882aec43d6e3ef75a78f80\) - Exact head: `17b81a1922a58df20e4beae21d1c6208048967ba` - Scenario: From a hidden\-activity tail, wheel upward100px to load two older messages\. Historical before and exact\-head after demonstrate preservation of the settled UI flow; real Gateway/RPC tests establish the invisible response\-metadata repair\. - Runtime/build: Fresh Control UI build from candidate tree e8bee624e15a6d16886aee0fd2eaff18e33324f6; 2641 served assets hashed\. - Input: Wheel upward100px over the thread - History requests: older\-80, older\-160, older\-180; zero numeric offsets - Result: Both older messages visible; no welcome panel - Same1280×480 viewport, scale1, light theme, en\-US, typed fixture and wheel input - Qualitative preservation comparison only; upstream boot/skeleton changes prevent pixel or startup\-timing claims - Source\-bound cursor requests and visible messages asserted by the existing normal history\-loading owners - Fresh build/capture tree equals the exact candidate tree
